Surah At-Tahrim is Madani [[Al-Suyuti, al-Durr al-Manthur, 8/213, citing Ibn al-Darib, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: "Surat al-Tahrim was revealed at Madinah." Ibn Mardawayh also related from Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr who said: "Surat al-Nisa' was revealed at Madinah, and (O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you) was revealed at Madinah."]] ﷽

* *

﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The occasion of its revelation: Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il [al-Bukhari] related to us, Ubayd Allah ibn Isma'il related to us, Abu Usamah related to us, from Hisham, from his father, from Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved sweets and honey, and when he had prayed the afternoon prayer (al-'Asr) he would go round to his wives and draw near to them. He entered upon Hafsah and remained with her longer than he usually did. I asked about that, and it was said to me: "A woman from her people had given her a jar of honey, and she gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a drink of it." I said: "By Allah, we shall certainly devise a plan against him." I mentioned that to Sawdah and said: "When he comes in to you, he will draw near to you, so say to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, have you eaten maghafir (a foul-smelling gum)?' He will say, 'No.' Then say to him: 'What is this smell?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked it greatly that a smell should be detected on him. He will say: 'Hafsah gave me a drink of honey.' Then say to him: 'Its bees must have grazed on the 'urfut (a bitter-smelling tree).' I shall say the same, and you too, O Safiyyah, say the same." When he entered upon Sawdah, Sawdah said: "By Allah, besides whom there is no god, I almost made him public with what you told me, and he was at the door out of fear of you." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ drew near, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, have you eaten maghafir?" He said: "No." I said: "Then what is this smell?" He said: "Hafsah gave me a drink of honey." She said: "Its bees must have grazed on the 'urfut." When he entered upon me I said to him the same, and when he entered upon Safiyyah she said to him the same. When he entered upon Hafsah she said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I not give you some of it to drink?" He said: "I have no need of it." Sawdah said: "Glory be to Allah, we have forbidden it to him!" I said to her: "Be quiet." [[Related by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter "Why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you," 9/374-375, and Muslim in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter on the obligation of expiation for one who forbids his wife without intending divorce, no. 1474, 2/1101-1102.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sabbah related to us, al-Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj who said: Ata claimed that he heard Ubayd ibn Umayr say: Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, was heard saying that the Prophet ﷺ would stay with Zaynab bint Jahsh and drink honey there. So I and Hafsah agreed that whichever of us the Prophet ﷺ entered upon first should say: "I smell maghafir from you; have you eaten maghafir?" He entered upon one of them and she said that to him. He said: "No harm. I drank honey at Zaynab bint Jahsh's, and I will not return to it." Then there was revealed: "O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives," up to His words: "If you two turn to Allah in repentance," concerning Aishah and Hafsah. And "When the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives" refers to his saying: "Rather, I drank honey." [[Related by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surat al-Tahrim, chapter "O Prophet, why do you forbid," 8/656; Muslim in Kitab al-Talaq, no. 1474, 2/1100; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 9/226.]]

With this same chain, he said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Ibrahim ibn Musa informed us, Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata with his chain, and he said: He said: "No, but I was drinking honey at Zaynab bint Jahsh's, and I will not return to it. I have sworn that you should not tell anyone of this, seeking thereby the pleasure of his wives." [[Related by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Talaq, chapter "Why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you," 9/374.]]

The commentators said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to divide his nights among his wives. When it was Hafsah's day, she asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to visit her father, and he permitted her. When she went out, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for his slave-girl Maryah the Copt, and he brought her into Hafsah's house, and he lay with her. When Hafsah returned, she found the door closed, so she sat at the door. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out with his face dripping with sweat, and Hafsah was weeping. He said: "What makes you weep?" She said: "You only gave me permission for this: you brought your slave-girl into my house, then you lay with her on my day and on my bed. Did you not see any respect or right for me? You would not do this with any of the other women." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Is she not my slave-girl whom Allah has made lawful for me? Be quiet; she is forbidden to me, seeking thereby your pleasure. Do not tell this to any of the women." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had gone out, Hafsah knocked on the wall between her and Aishah and said: "Shall I not give you good news? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has forbidden his slave-girl Maryah to himself, and Allah has relieved us of her." She informed Aishah of what she had seen. They were close allies, supporting each other against the rest of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. Aishah became angry, and she did not stop at the Prophet of Allah ﷺ until he swore that he would not approach her. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: [[See al-Tabari 28/157, Ibn Kathir 4/387, and al-Durr al-Manthur 8/216-217.]] "O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you" — meaning the honey and Maryah — "seeking the pleasure of your wives. Allah is Forgiving and Merciful," and He commanded him to expiate his oath and to take back his slave-girl. So he said:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 66, verses 2–3:

﴿God has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths (taḥillat aymānikum)﴾, meaning He has made clear and made obligatory that you expiate them (kaffara, expiation) when you break them (ḥanitum), and this is what is mentioned in Surat al-Ma'ida. ﴿God is your Protector (mawlākum)﴾, your Guardian and your Helper. ﴿And He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.﴾

The scholars differed concerning the wording of prohibition (tahrīm). Some people said: it is not an oath (yamīn, a binding oath). So if a man says to his wife, "You are forbidden to me (anti 'alayya ḥarām)," or "I have forbidden you (ḥarramtuki)," then if he intends by it divorce, it is divorce; if he intends by it zihar (the pre-Islamic repudiation formula), it is zihar. If he intends the prohibition of her person, or says it without specifying an intention, then he owes the expiation of an oath by the mere utterance itself. If he says this to his slave-girl, then if he intends manumission, she is freed; if he intends the prohibition of her person, or says it without specifying, then he owes the expiation of an oath. If he says of food, "I have forbidden it to myself," then nothing is owed by him. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, and al-Shafi'i adopted it.

A group went to the view that it is an oath. So if he says that to his wife [168/b] or to his slave-girl, then the expiation is not obligatory upon him as long as he has not come near her, just as if he had sworn that he would not have intercourse with her. If he forbids food, it is like swearing that he will not eat it, so there is no expiation for him as long as he has not eaten it. This is narrated from Abu Bakr and 'A'isha, and al--Awza'i and Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, also said so.

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, who was informed by Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, who was informed by Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, who said: Mu'adh ibn Fadala narrated to us, who said: Hisham narrated to us from Yahya, from Ibn Hakim, and he is Ya'la ibn Hakim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said concerning "the forbidden" (al-ḥarām): he makes expiation. And Ibn 'Abbas said: "Indeed you have in the Messenger of God an excellent example" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, the chapter of Surat al-Tahrim, the section on "O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you..." 8/656, and by Muslim in Talaq, the chapter on the obligation of expiation upon one who forbids his wife and does not intend divorce, no. (1473) 2/1100.]] [Al-Ahzab: 21].

﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement (ḥadīthan)﴾, which was his prohibiting his slave-girl upon himself, and his saying to Hafsa: "Do not inform anyone of this."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: He confided the matter of the caliphate after him, and Hafsa then related it. [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/219 as narrated by Ibn Mardawayh.]] Al-Kalbi said: He confided to her that your father and the father of 'A'isha would be two caliphs over my community after me. Maymun ibn Mihran said: He confided that Abu Bakr would be my caliph after me. [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/218 as narrated by Ibn 'Asakir, and whatever is reported by him alone is weak.]]

﴿Then when she informed of it﴾, that is, Hafsa informed 'A'isha, ﴿and God made him aware of it﴾, meaning God Most High informed His Prophet that she had disclosed it. ﴿He made known part of it﴾. 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and al-Kisa'i read "'arrafa" (عَرَفَ) with a light (unshadda) rā', meaning: he made known part of the act she had committed by divulging his secret, that is, he became angry with her for that and requited her for it, from the saying of one who says to someone who wronged him: "I will surely make you know what you have done," meaning: I will requite you for it. He requited her for it by divorcing her. When this reached 'Umar, he said: "If there were any good in the family of al-Khattab, the Messenger of God would not have divorced you." Then Gabriel came and commanded him to take her back, and the Messenger of God ﷺ withdrew from his wives for a month and sat in the upper room of Umm Ibrahim Maria, until the verse of choice was revealed. [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (175): "I have not seen it in this form; it is in al-Hakim and others without mention of its cause."]]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The Messenger of God ﷺ did not divorce Hafsa; he merely intended to divorce her, then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said: "Do not divorce her, for she is one who fasts much and prays much at night, and she is among your wives in Paradise." So he did not divorce her.

The others read "'arrafa" (عَرَّفَ) with the doubled rā' (shadda), meaning: he made Hafsa aware of that statement afterwards, that is, he informed her of some of the words that had come from her.

﴿And he disregarded part of it﴾, meaning he did not make her aware of it and did not inform her of it. Al-Hasan said: "A noble person never probes to the end." God Most High said: ﴿He made known part of it and disregarded part of it﴾. [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/219 as narrated by Ibn Mardawayh from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him.]] This was because when the Prophet ﷺ saw the displeasure in Hafsa's face, he wished to placate her, so he confided to her two matters: the prohibition of the slave-girl upon himself, and the good news that the caliphate after him would be (held) by Abu Bakr and by her father 'Umar, may God be pleased with her. Then Hafsa informed 'A'isha, and God Most High made His Prophet aware of it. He made Hafsa aware of part of it, and informed her of some of what 'A'isha had reported to her, namely the prohibition of the slave-girl, and he disregarded part of it, meaning the mention of the caliphate, for the Messenger of God ﷺ disliked that this should spread among the people. ﴿So when he informed her of it﴾, that is, the Prophet informed Hafsa of what God had made him aware of, ﴿she said﴾, Hafsa, ﴿"Who told you this?"﴾, that is: Who informed you that I divulged the secret? ﴿He said: "The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me."﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 66, verse 4:

﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah﴾, meaning: from colluding against the Prophet ﷺ with harm. He addresses Aisha and Hafsa. ﴿Then indeed your hearts have inclined﴾, meaning: they deviated and turned away from the truth, and you two deserve repentance. Ibn Zayd said: their hearts inclined in that they were pleased by what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked, namely abstaining from his concubine.

Akhbarana ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, akhbarana Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi, akhbarana Muhammad ibn Yusuf, haddathana Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari), haddathana Abu al-Yaman, akhbarana Shu'ayb, from al-Zuhri, akhbarani ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Thawr, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbbas, who said: I had continually been eager to ask ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab about the two wives of the Prophet ﷺ concerning whom Allah the Exalted said to them: "If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined," until he performed the pilgrimage and I performed it with him. He veered off, and I veered off with him carrying a water-skin. He relieved himself, then came back, and I poured water over his hands from it, and he performed ablution. I said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, who are the two wives of the Prophet ﷺ concerning whom Allah the Exalted said: 'If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined'?" He said: "How astonishing you are, O Ibn ʿAbbas! They are ʿAisha and Hafsa."

Then ʿUmar began the narration, continuing it, saying: "I and a neighbour of mine from the Ansar in the clan of Banu Umayya ibn Zayd, which is in the upper parts of Medina, used to take turns descending to the Prophet ﷺ. He would descend one day and I would descend one day. When I descended, I brought him news of what had occurred that day of revelation or other matters, and when he descended he did likewise.

We, the tribe of Quraysh, used to dominate women, but when we came to the Ansar we found they were a people whose women dominated them. Our women began to learn from the manners of the Ansar's women. I shouted at my wife and she answered me back, and I disapproved of her answering me back. She said: 'Why do you disapprove of my answering you back? By Allah, the wives of the Prophet ﷺ answer him back, and one of them may abandon him until nightfall.' This alarmed me and I said: 'Whoever among them does that has failed.'

Then I gathered my clothes [and descended] [[Addition from "B".]] and entered upon Hafsa and said to her: 'O Hafsa, does one of you anger the Prophet ﷺ until nightfall today?' She said: 'Yes.' I said: 'You have failed and lost. Do you feel secure that Allah the Exalted may become angry because of the anger of His Messenger, and you be destroyed? Do not ask the Prophet ﷺ for too much, do not answer him back in anything, do not abandon him, and ask me whatever you wish. Do not let it deceive you that she [your neighbour] [[In "B" "your concubine".]] [is more beautiful] [[In "A" "more pleasing".]] than you and more beloved to the Prophet ﷺ' — meaning ʿAisha."

ʿUmar said: "We had heard that the Ghassanids were shoeing their horses to attack us. My Ansari companion descended on his turn, then returned to us at night and struck my door violently and said: 'Is he there?'

I was alarmed and went out to him. He said: 'A great matter has occurred today.' I said: 'What is it? Has the Ghassan come?' He said: 'No, rather something greater and more dreadful: the Prophet ﷺ has divorced his wives.' I said: 'Hafsa has failed and lost. I used to think this was about to happen.'

I gathered my clothes and prayed the dawn prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered his upper chamber and secluded himself there. I entered upon Hafsa and found her weeping. I said: 'What makes you weep? Did I not warn you? Has the Prophet ﷺ divorced you?'

She said: 'I do not know. Here he is, secluded in the upper chamber.' I came to the pulpit and found around it a group, some of whom were weeping. I sat with them briefly, then what I felt overcame me, so I came to the upper chamber where the Prophet ﷺ was, and I said to a black servant of his: 'Ask permission for ʿUmar.' He entered, spoke to the Prophet ﷺ, then returned and said: 'I spoke to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned you to him, but he remained silent.' So I left and sat with the group near the pulpit. Then what I felt overcame me again, so I came to the servant and said: 'Ask permission.' He asked permission, then returned to me and said: 'I mentioned you to him and he remained silent.' [So I returned and sat with the group near the pulpit. Then what I felt overcame me again, so I came to the servant and said: 'Ask permission for ʿUmar,' and he asked permission, then returned to me and said: 'I mentioned you to him and he remained silent.'] [[Addition from "B".]]

When I turned away departing, behold, the servant called me and said: 'The Prophet ﷺ has given you permission.' I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and found him reclining on a mat of palm fibres, with no bedding between him and it, the mat having left its marks on his side, leaning on a leather cushion stuffed with palm fibre. I greeted him, then said while standing: 'O Messenger of Allah, have you divorced your wives?' He raised his gaze to me and said: 'No.' I said: 'Allah is Most Great!' Then I said, standing and seeking to be sociable: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only you had seen me, when we, the tribe of Quraysh, used to dominate women, but when we came to Medina we found a people whom their women dominated.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled. Then I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only you had seen me when I entered upon Hafsa and said to her: "Do not let it deceive you that your neighbour [is more beautiful] [[In "A" "more pleasing".]] than you and more beloved to the Prophet ﷺ" — meaning ʿAisha.' The Prophet ﷺ smiled another smile. I sat down when I saw him smiling, and I raised my gaze around his house, and by Allah I saw nothing in it that would hold the gaze except three hides. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah that He may widen provision for your community, for Persia and Byzantium have been given abundance and have been granted of worldly things, while they do not worship Allah.'

The Prophet ﷺ sat up, for he had been reclining, and said: '"Are you in this state, O son of al-Khattab? Those people have had their good things hastened in the life of this world."'

I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, ask forgiveness for me.'

The Prophet ﷺ had withdrawn from his wives because of that matter, which Hafsa had disclosed to ʿAisha, for twenty-nine nights. He had said: 'I will not enter upon them for a month,' out of the intensity of his displeasure with them when Allah the Mighty and Majestic rebuked him.

When twenty-nine nights had passed, he entered upon ʿAisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and began with her. ʿAisha said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, you had sworn that you would not enter upon us for a month, and now we have entered the twenty-ninth night, counting them one by one!' He said: 'The month is twenty-nine,' and that month was twenty-nine nights.

ʿAisha said: 'Then Allah sent down the option (of choice), and he began with me, the first of his wives, and I chose him. Then he offered choice to all his wives, and they all said the same as ʿAisha said.' [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Mazalim, bab al-Ghurfa wa al-ʿaliya al-mushrifa wa ghayr al-mushrifa fi al-suţuh wa ghayriha: 5/114-116, the wording is his, and Muslim in al-Talaq, bab fi al-iila' wa i'tizal al-nisa' wa takhyirihinna wa qawlihi ta'ala (wa in tazahara 'alayhi), no. (1479), 2/1111-1113.]]

Akhbarana ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi, akhbarana Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi, akhbarana Muhammad ibn Yusuf, haddathana Muhammad ibn Isma'il, haddathana Abu al-Yaman, akhbarana Shu'ayb, from al-Zuhri, akhbarani Abu Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman that ʿAisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, informed him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to her when Allah commanded him to give his wives the choice. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ began with me and said: 'I am about to mention a matter to you, so there is no harm for you [in not hurrying] [[In "A" "(that you should not hasten)".]] until you consult your two parents.' He knew that my parents would never command me to part from him. She said: Then he said: 'Indeed Allah said: "O Prophet, say to your wives..."' up to the completion of the two verses. I said: 'Should I consult my parents about this? Rather, I desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode.' [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surat al-Ahzab, bab (Qul li-azwajika in kuntunna turidna al-hayat al-dunya wa zinatuha fa-ta'alayna umatti'kunna wa usarrihkunna sarahan jamila): 8/519.]]

Akhbarana Isma'il ibn ʿAbd al-Qahir, akhbarana ʿAbd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad, akhbarana Muhammad ibn ʿIsa, haddathana Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan, haddathana Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, haddathani Zuhayr ibn Harb, haddathana ʿUmar ibn Yunus al-Hanafi, haddathana ʿIkrima ibn ʿAmmar, from Simak [ibn Zumayl] [[Thus in "A", while in "B" "Ibn Abi Zumayl", and both are wrong; the correct form is "Abi Zumayl", as in al-Tahdhib and in Muslim.]] who said: Ibn ʿAbbas narrated to us, saying: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab narrated to me, saying: When the Prophet ﷺ withdrew from his wives, and he mentioned the narration. He said: I entered upon him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is it that burdens you concerning the matter of women? If you have divorced them, then Allah is with you, and His angels, and Jibril and Mika'il, and I and Abu Bakr and the believers are with you." I seldom spoke, praising Allah the Exalted, without hoping that Allah would confirm what I was saying. And this verse was revealed: "It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you." "And if you two back each other against him, then indeed Allah is his protector, and Jibril and the righteous believers, and the angels after that are supporters." [[Part of a long hadith narrated by Muslim in al-Talaq, bab fi al-iila' wa i'tizal al-nisa' wa takhyirihinna ... no. (1479), 2/1105-1108.]]

His words: ﴿And if you two back each other against him﴾, meaning: you two support one another and cooperate in harming the Prophet ﷺ. The people of Kufa read (tazahara) with the letter ẓāʾ lightened, and the others with it doubled.

﴿Then indeed Allah is his protector﴾, meaning his guardian and helper; ﴿and Jibril and the righteous believers﴾. It is related from Ibn Masʿud and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that ﴿the righteous believers﴾ means Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both. [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/223 to Ibn ʿAsakir, and he indicated in the introduction to al-Jami' that attribution to Ibn ʿAsakir signals weakness.]] Al-Kalbi said: they are the sincere ones who are not hypocrites.

﴿And the angels after that are supporters﴾. Muqatil said: after Allah and Jibril, "and the righteous believers and the angels after that are supporters", meaning: helpers of the Prophet ﷺ. This is from the singular used in place of the plural, like His saying: "And excellent are those as companions" [An-Nisa: 69].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 66, verse 5:

﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you, submitting (muslimat), believing (mu'minat), devoutly obedient (qanitat), repentant (ta'ibat), worshipping ('abidat), traveling (sa'ihat), previously married (thayyibat) and virgins (abkaran)﴾. That is: it is obligatory from Allah, if His Messenger divorces you, that He will substitute for him wives better than you, ﴿submitting﴾ (muslimat) meaning humbling themselves before Allah in obedience, ﴿believing﴾ (mu'minat) meaning affirming the Oneness of Allah, ﴿devoutly obedient﴾ (qanitat) meaning obedient. It is also said: supplicating (da'iyat). It is also said: praying (musalliyat). ﴿Repentant, worshipping, traveling﴾ (sa'ihat) meaning fasting (sa'imat). Zayd ibn Aslam said: emigrating (muhajirat). It is also said: they will travel with him wherever he travels. ﴿Previously married and virgins﴾. This is a report about capability, not about actual occurrence, because He said: "if he divorces you," while He knew that he would not divorce them. This is like His saying: "And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, then they will not be like you" [Muhammad: 38]. This is a report about capability, because there is no nation in existence better than the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 66, verses 6–8:

His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is men and stones, over which are angels, harsh and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded.﴾ ﴿O you who have disbelieved, do not make excuses today. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾ ﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance.﴾

Ata reported from Ibn Abbas: that is, by refraining from what Allah has forbidden you and acting in obedience to Him. ﴿And your families from a Fire﴾ means: command them to do good, forbid them from evil, teach them and discipline them, so that by this you protect them from the Fire. ﴿Whose fuel is men and stones﴾ ... ﴿over which are angels﴾ means the guardians of the Fire (khazanat al-nar). ﴿Harsh﴾ means rough and stern toward the people of the Fire. ﴿Severe﴾ means strong; one of them pushes with a single thrust seventy thousand into the Fire, and they are the Zabaniyah. Allah has not placed mercy within them.

﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them and do what they are commanded.﴾ ﴿O you who have disbelieved, do not make excuses today. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance.﴾ Qara'a al-Hasan and Abu Bakr, from Asim, read "nusuhan" with a dammah on the nun, while the majority read it with a fatha, meaning: a repentance possessing sincerity (nush), which counsels its owner to abstain from returning to what he repented of.

The scholars differed regarding its meaning. Umar, Ubayy and Mu'adh said: "Sincere repentance" is that one repents and then does not return to the sin, just as milk does not return to the udder. [[Ibn Hajar said in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah (3/390): Ahmad ibn Mani' reported it in his Musnad, and its chain is sound and mawquf (halting at a companion). It was also narrated by al-Tabari (28/167).]]

Al-Hasan said: It is that the servant is remorseful over what has passed, resolved not to return to it. [[Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/227) to Abd ibn Humayd.]]

Al-Kalbi said: That one seeks forgiveness with the tongue, regrets with the heart, and refrains with the body.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: A repentance by which you counsel your own souls.

Al-Qurazi said: It comprises four things: seeking forgiveness with the tongue, ceasing with the limbs, resolving not to return with the heart, and abandoning evil companions.

﴿It may be that your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow, on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him.﴾ That is, Allah will not punish them by entering the Fire. ﴿Their light will run before them and on their right﴾ over the Sirat. ﴿They will say﴾ when the light of the hypocrites is extinguished: ﴿Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us; indeed You are over all things Competent.﴾

Then Allah struck a parable for the righteous men and righteous women among the women, so He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah﴾, and her name was Wa'ilah, ﴿and the wife of Lot﴾, and her name was Wahilah. Muqatil said: Wali'ah and Wali'hah.

﴿They were under two of Our righteous servants﴾, and they are Noah and Lot, peace be upon them, ﴿but they betrayed them﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: No wife of a prophet ever committed adultery; rather, their betrayal was that they were upon a religion other than their husbands' religion. The wife of Noah would tell the people, "He is a madman," and whenever anyone believed in him, she would inform the tyrants about him. As for the wife of Lot, she would direct his people to his guests: whenever a guest arrived at night, she would kindle the fire, and whenever a guest arrived by day, she would produce smoke so that his people would know that a guest had arrived.

Al-Kalbi said: They concealed hypocrisy and displayed faith.

﴿But they availed them nothing against Allah at all﴾, meaning they did not avert from them the punishment of Allah despite their being prophets' wives. ﴿And it was said: Enter the Fire along with those who enter.﴾

By this verse Allah cut off the hope of everyone who engages in disobedience that the righteousness of others will benefit him.

Then Allah struck a parable for the righteous men and righteous women among the women, so He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah﴾, and her name was Wa'ilah, ﴿and the wife of Lot﴾, and her name was Wahilah. Then he informed that the disobedience of another does not harm a person when he is obedient, so he said: ﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾, and she is Asiya bint Muzahim.

The commentators (al-Mufassirun) said: When Musa overcame the magicians, the wife of Pharaoh believed. When Pharaoh became aware of her conversion, he fastened her hands and feet with four stakes and cast her out into the sun.

Salman said: The wife of Pharaoh was being tormented by the sun, and when they withdrew from her, the angels would shade her.[[Narrated by al-Tabari (28/171) and Abu Ya'la (6/53). Ibn Hajar said in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah (3/390): sahih, mawquf (a report traced to a Companion).]]

﴿When she said: My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾. So Allah uncovered for her her house in Paradise until she saw it.

In the narrative: Pharaoh ordered a huge rock to be brought to be dropped upon her. When they brought the rock to her, she said: "My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise." Then she saw her house in Paradise, made of white pearl, and her soul was taken, and the rock was dropped upon a body with no soul in it, and she felt no pain.

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: Allah raised the wife of Pharaoh up to Paradise, and she is there eating and drinking.

﴿And save me from Pharaoh and his deed﴾. Muqatil said: "and his deed" means shirk (associating partners with Allah). Abu Salih reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning "and his deed" that he said: "its intercourse" (jimā'uhu).

﴿And save me from the wrongdoing people﴾: the disbelievers.

﴿And Maryam daughter of 'Imran, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it﴾: meaning into the opening of her shirt (jaib dir'iha), and for this reason the pronoun is feminine-referring as a metaphor (al-kinaya). ﴿of Our Spirit, and she affirmed the words of her Lord﴾: meaning the laws which Allah prescribed for His servants through His words that were revealed ﴿and His books﴾. The readers of Basra and Hafs read "wa-kutubihi" in the plural, while the others read "wa-kitabihi" in the singular. Its intended meaning is also plurality. And by "His books" he meant those revealed to Ibrahim, Musa, Dawud and 'Isa, peace be upon them.

﴿And she was among the obedient (al-qanitin)﴾: meaning among the obedient people devoted to her Lord, and for this reason it does not say "min al-qanitat" (feminine plural).

'Ata' said: "min al-qanitin" means among those who pray. It is also possible that by "al-qanitin" is meant her kinsfolk and clan, for they were people of righteousness, obedient to Allah.
